title: Descent of prime monomial factors through a lattice-support retraction
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative domain and $R\subset D$ a unital subring. Regard $R\subset D$ also as an $R$-submodule [def-weil-submodule-span]. Let $r\ge0$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in D$ be nonzero prime nonunits, and for $a\in\mathbf N^r$ put $x^a=\prod_{i=1}^r x_i^{a_i}$. Prime means that $x_i\mid ab$ implies $x_i\mid a$ or $x_i\mid b$. Let $M\subset\mathbf Z^r$ be an additive subgroup such that $x^a\in R$ for every $a\in M\cap\mathbf N^r$. Suppose there is an $R$-linear map $\rho:D\to R$ restricting to the identity on $R$, satisfying $\rho(x^a)=0$ whenever $a\in\mathbf N^r\setminus M$, and satisfying $\rho(v)\in R^\times$ for every $v\in D^\times$. Suppose there is $w\in M\cap\mathbf N^r$ with all coordinates strictly positive (vacuously so if $r=0$). Then for every $s\in M\cap\mathbf N^r$ and $h,h'\in R$ with $hh'=x^s$ there exist $e\in M\cap\mathbf N^r$ with $e\le s$ coordinatewise, $v\in D^\times$ and $u\in R^\times$ such that $h=x^e v$ in $D$, $u=\rho(v)$ and $h=x^e u$ in $R$. The zero exponent $s=0$ and the empty coordinate set $r=0$ are included; no factoriality of $R$ or $D$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-prime-product-factor-splitting] with $a=1$ and with finite index set $J=\{(i,j):1\le i\le r,\ 0\le j<s_i\}$, assigning $p_{(i,j)}=x_i$. Its product is $x^s$, since the $i$th block has $s_i$ copies of $x_i$. The hypotheses are exactly the assumed primality of each $x_i$ and $hh'=x^s$ in $D$. Obtain a partition $T\sqcup U=J$, elements $b,c\in D$ with $bc=1$, and $h=b\prod_{(i,j)\in T}x_i$. Put $e_i=\#\{j:(i,j)\in T\}$. Then $0\le e_i\le s_i$ and regrouping the finite product gives $h=x^e v$, where $v=b\in D^\times$ has inverse $c$. No distinctness or nonassociation of the $x_i$ was used.

proof.text: Put $N=\sum_i e_i$ and $a_i=Nw_i-e_i$. Every $w_i\ge1$, so $Nw_i\ge N\ge e_i$; hence $a\in\mathbf N^r$, $a+e=Nw$ and $x^a h=x^{Nw}v$. Also $Nw\in M$ and $x^{Nw}\in R$ by the hypotheses. In the group $\mathbf Z^r$, if $e\notin M$ then $a\notin M$, since $a\in M$ would imply $e=Nw-a\in M$.

proof.text: Suppose $e\notin M$. Step 2 gives $a\notin M$, so the stated support condition gives $\rho(x^a)=0$. Because $h\in R$ and $\rho$ is $R$-linear, $\rho(x^a h)=h\rho(x^a)=0$. On the other hand, $x^{Nw}\in R$ and the equality in step 2 give $\rho(x^a h)=\rho(x^{Nw}v)=x^{Nw}\rho(v)$. This is nonzero in $D$: a finite product of powers of nonzero $x_i$ is nonzero in a domain, and $\rho(v)$ is a unit of the subring $R$, hence also of $D$. This contradiction proves $e\in M$. Each equality uses only scalar linearity, with its scalar explicitly in $R$.

proof.text: Now $x^e\in R$. Apply $\rho$ to $h=x^e v$ to obtain $h=\rho(h)=x^e\rho(v)$ in $R$, since $\rho$ fixes $R$. Set $u=\rho(v)\in R^\times$, using the assumed unit preservation. Together with $e\le s$ and the equality in $D$ from step 1, this proves all clauses. If $s=0$ then $J=\varnothing$ and $e=0$; if $r=0$, all vectors are empty, $N=0$ and every monomial is $1$. The same formulas apply in both cases.
